mainTopic: Brothers sharing an inheritance: which gains, costs, and wedding-gift debts are shared and which belong to one brother alone.
overview: The משנה teaches that when brothers keep their inheritance together as partners, a brother drafted into the king's service shares the result with everyone, but a sick brother pays for his own healing. A ברייתא adds that a brother appointed tax collector or officer shares the profit if he was chosen because of the family, even if he is the sharpest of them. Another ברייתא says a brother who leaves to learn תורה or a trade gets support only when he is home. The גמרא concludes that he still gets what he would have cost at home. רבין in the name of רבי אלעא limits the medical rule to illness from carelessness, such as catching cold, based on רבי חנינא. A new משנה rules that שושבינות (groomsman gifts) from the father's lifetime is shared by the brothers, because a court can collect it. A ברייתא seems to contradict this, and the גמרא gives three answers: רבי יוחנן's, רבי אסי's, and שמואל's, which is about a יבם. The גמרא then challenges שמואל using a ruling of his own about returning קידושין money, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: shared service, private medical costs
steps.stepSummary: Brothers who are partners: if one is drafted to service, it counts for everyone. If one gets sick, he pays for his own healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Brothers who are partners, where one of them was drafted into service, he was drafted from the shared pot. If he got sick and was healed, he was healed from his own money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two quick rules for brothers who keep their inheritance together as אחין השותפין: drafted service is shared, and medical costs are private.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Falling to the middle' means the gains or losses from his service go into the shared pot for all the brothers. Sickness is different: it is personal to the one brother, so the cost of healing comes from his own share.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (marks the start of the משנה text)
Brothers who are partners, keeping the inheritance together
Service or a job; here, drafted service
Literally 'fell to the middle', meaning it belongs to the shared pot

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole topic: which things that happen to one partner-brother count as shared business, and which count as private.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Brothers who are partners
where one of them was drafted into service
he was drafted from the middle (the shared pot).
If he became sick and was healed,
he was healed at his own expense.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drafted service of one partner-brother is a shared matter, while his medical expenses are his own.

steps.title: Defining the service: the king's service
steps.stepSummary: A teaching explains that the 'service' in the משנה means forced service to the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: this 'service' means the king's service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining one word in the משנה: the אומנות the brother 'fell into' is service forced on him by the king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the משנה's rule. It is about service the government forces on the family, not a job the brother chooses for himself. That is why it counts as shared.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא (marks the start of the discussion)
It was taught (introduces a teaching from the time of the משנה)
The king's service, forced government duty

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
This 'service' means the king's service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a key term in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's 'service' is forced royal service.

steps.title: A brother appointed tax collector or officer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if a brother is appointed גבאי or פולמוסטוס because of the family, the profit is shared; if because of himself, it is his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One of the brothers who was appointed tax collector or army officer: if it was because of the brothers, the profit goes to the brothers; if it was because of himself, it goes to himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a similar case: a brother gets a profitable government job. Who gets the profit depends on why he was picked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is the reason for the appointment. If the government picked someone to represent the family, the job belongs to the family. If they picked him personally, it is his.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One of the brothers whom they appointed
tax collector or army commander:
if it was because of the brothers, it goes to the brothers;
phrases.notes: 'Because of the brothers' means he was taken as the family's representative.

phrases.english: if it was because of himself, it goes to himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין שֶׁמִּינּוּהוּ גַּבַּאי אוֹ פּוּלְמוֹסְטוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ברייתא about a government appointment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Profit from a government appointment follows the reason for it: family-based means shared, personal means private.

steps.title: Isn't the first half obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if he was appointed because of the brothers, of course the profit is theirs. Why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was because of the brothers, it goes to the brothers: that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's first rule as too obvious to need saying. This sets up the next step, which will show what the rule really teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the family was the reason for the appointment, it seems plain that the family shares the profit. A ברייתא should not waste words, so the גמרא looks for the new point hidden in this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a rule teaches nothing new)

phrases.english: If it was because of the brothers, it goes to the brothers:
that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא's first clause
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a family-based appointment's profit goes to all the brothers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems self-evident, so why would the ברייתא need to state it?

steps.title: The case of the sharper brother
steps.stepSummary: The rule is needed when the appointed brother is sharper than the others. We might think his talent earned him the job, so the ברייתא teaches that the profit is still shared.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he is sharper. You might have said his sharpness caused it; so it teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the rule is needed for a brother who is more capable than the rest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the appointed brother is the sharpest, we might think his own skill got him picked, so the profit should be his alone. The ברייתא teaches that if the appointment was really on the family's account, the profit is shared even so.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a special case)
You might have said (introduces a wrong first thought)

steps.whatToRemember: A brother picked to represent the family shares the profit with his brothers, even if he is the most talented of them.
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not mean that skill never matters. If he was appointed because of himself, the profit is his. The point here is that skill alone does not override a family-based appointment.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he is sharper;
you might have said:
his sharpness caused it for him,
so it teaches us that it is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the rule in a special case where it is not obvious
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the appointed brother is sharper, his skill caused the appointment, so the profit is his.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the appointment was on the family's account, the profit is shared despite his sharpness.

steps.title: A brother who left to learn Torah or a trade
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a brother who took 200 זוז to go and learn תורה or a trade can be told by the brothers that he gets support only if he is with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One of the brothers who took two hundred זוז to learn תורה or to learn a trade, the brothers can say to him: If you are with us, you get food; if you are not with us, you do not get food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a brother who took money from the shared funds to go away and learn. The brothers can limit his support to when he is with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another case of what counts as shared and what counts as personal. Food for a brother who lives with them is a shared cost, but the brothers can refuse to fund his living away from them.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין שֶׁנָּטַל מָאתַיִם זוּז
phrases.english: One of the brothers who took two hundred zuz
to learn Torah or to learn a trade:
the brothers can say to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה אֶצְלֵנוּ – יֵשׁ לְךָ מְזוֹנוֹת,
phrases.english: If you are with us, you get food;

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵין אַתָּה אֶצְלֵנוּ – אֵין לְךָ מְזוֹנוֹת.
phrases.english: if you are not with us, you do not get food.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶחָד מִן הָאַחִין שֶׁנָּטַל מָאתַיִם זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא on a related partnership question
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Brothers may limit a partner-brother's support from the shared funds to when he is with them.

steps.title: Why not support him wherever he is?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: why can the brothers refuse to support him unless he lives with them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them give him support wherever he is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ruling from Step 6. Why should it matter where the brother lives? He is a partner in the estate either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brother is an heir, so he seems to deserve his share of support. The ברייתא's condition, 'only if you are with us,' looks unfair, and the גמרא wants a reason for it.

phrases.english: But let them give him [support] wherever he is!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the condition in the ברייתא of Step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the brother gets support only if he stays with the brothers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: As an heir he should be entitled to support no matter where he lives

steps.title: Living together costs less
steps.stepSummary: The ruling supports רב הונא, who says a household gets more blessing when many people live in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב הונא, for רב הונא said: the blessing of a house comes with its many members.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that supporting a brother away from home costs more. When many people live together, each person costs less.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב הונא's principle, shared living saves money. The brothers do not have to pay the extra cost of separate living, and that explains the ברייתא's condition.

phrases.english: This supports רב הונא,
for רב הונא said:
The blessing of a house is in its abundance.
phrases.notes: He means that when many people live together, there is more to go around and each one costs less.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a practical reason for the condition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The brother should get support anywhere
steps.terutzMaskana: Separate living costs more, so the brothers need not pay for it

steps.title: At least give him what he would cost at home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: then why not give him the amount he would cost if he lived at home?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them give him according to the blessing of the house!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further. Even if he can't get the full cost of living alone, he should at least get what he would cost at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's principle only explains why he doesn't get the higher amount. It does not explain why he should get nothing at all.

phrases.english: But let them give him according to the blessing of the house!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the answer of Step 8 goes
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that he gets no support at all when away
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא's principle only blocks the extra cost, not the basic share

steps.title: Yes, he gets the home amount
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: he does receive what he would have cost at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, so it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the point. The brother away from home gets the amount he would cost if he lived with them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the ברייתא only means he does not get the extra cost of separate living. His basic share of support stays.
steps.whatToRemember: A brother who leaves the shared home gets support equal to what he would cost at home, but not the extra cost of living alone.

phrases.english: Indeed, so it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He might get nothing while away
steps.terutzMaskana: He gets the amount he would cost at home

steps.title: Medical costs: only illness from carelessness is his own
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a sick brother pays for his own treatment; רבין in the name of רבי אלעא limits this to illness caused by carelessness.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] If he became sick and was healed, he is healed at his own expense. רבין sent in the name of רבי אלעא: this was taught only when he got sick through carelessness, but if it was beyond his control, he is healed from the shared estate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and adds a limit to it. A brother pays his own medical bills only if the illness was his own fault.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this teaching, we might think every illness is a private expense. רבי אלעא divides it: illness from carelessness is paid from his own pocket, and illness beyond his control is paid from the shared estate.

phrases.english: If he became sick and was healed –
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה about the brothers sharing an estate.

phrases.english: he is healed from his own [money].
רבין sent in the name of רבי אלעא:
They taught this only when he became sick through carelessness,
but if it was beyond his control –
he is healed from the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רָבִין מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אִלְעָא לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only illness from carelessness is paid privately; illness beyond one's control is paid from the estate

steps.title: What counts as carelessness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of illness counts as coming through carelessness.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of carelessness?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition. How can a person be at fault for getting sick?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Illness usually seems to come from Heaven. The גמרא needs to show which illnesses a person brings on himself.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is the case of carelessness?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to define a term from Step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which illnesses count as caused by carelessness

steps.title: Colds and traps are a person's own fault
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי חנינא, everything is from Heaven except colds and traps, which a careful person can avoid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חנינא said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except colds and traps, as it says: 'Colds and traps are on the path of the crooked; one who guards his soul keeps far from them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רבי חנינא's teaching. Getting sick from cold, or getting hurt by dangers you could have avoided, counts as carelessness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most things that happen to a person are from Heaven, so they count as beyond his control. Colds and traps are different, because the פסוק says a careful person stays away from them. So illness from these is his own fault.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything is in the hands of Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: A brother pays his own medical costs only for avoidable illness, like catching cold. Other illness is paid from the shared estate.

phrases.english: As [taught by] רבי חנינא –
for רבי חנינא said:
Everything is in the hands of Heaven,
except for colds and traps;
as it is said: 'Colds and traps are on the path of the crooked,'
'one who guards his soul keeps far from them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Illness from cold or avoidable dangers counts as carelessness, based on רבי חנינא and the פסוק in משלי

steps.title: New משנה: wedding gifts go back to all the brothers
steps.stepSummary: שושבינות from the father's lifetime is shared by all the brothers when it is repaid, because it can be collected in court; gifts of wine and oil cannot be collected.
steps.simpleTranslation: Brothers, some of whom gave שושבינות during their father's lifetime: when the שושבינות comes back, it goes back to the shared estate, because שושבינות can be collected in court. But one who sends his friend jugs of wine or jugs of oil cannot collect them in court, because they are acts of kindness.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about שושבינות, gifts given to help a groom with his wedding that are expected to be repaid. It rules that these debts belong to the whole estate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שושבינות is treated like a real loan that a בית דין can enforce, so it is part of the father's estate and is shared. Simple gifts like wine or oil are just kindness, so no one can demand them back in court.

keyTerms.meaning: Wedding gifts from groomsmen, expected to be returned

steps.confusionAlert: שושבינות is not a plain gift. It works like a loan: when you get married, the one who received it must give it back.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הָאַחִין שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִקְצָתָן שׁוֹשְׁבִינוּת בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב,
phrases.english: MISHNA: Brothers, some of whom gave שושבינות during the father's lifetime,
when the שושבינות came back –
it comes back to the middle;
because שושבינות is collected in court.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַשּׁוֹלֵחַ לַחֲבֵירוֹ כַּדֵּי יַיִן וְכַדֵּי שֶׁמֶן –
phrases.english: But one who sends his friend jugs of wine and jugs of oil –
they are not collected in court,
because they are acts of kindness.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאַחִין שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִקְצָתָן שׁוֹשְׁבִינוּת בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שושבינות is a debt the court enforces and belongs to the shared estate; gifts of kindness are not enforceable

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say it goes to the son alone
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says שושבינות the father sent through his son returns to that son alone, which seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a contradiction was raised: If his father sent שושבינות for him, when it comes back, it comes back to him. If שושבינות was sent to his father, when it is repaid, it is repaid from the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with the משנה. The ברייתא says the son keeps what comes back, but the משנה said it goes to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's first case, the father sent שושבינות on behalf of a son, and the return belongs to that son. That seems to contradict the משנה's ruling that the return is shared. The ברייתא's second case, שושבינות sent to the father, is repaid from the shared estate.

phrases.english: GEMARA: And a contradiction was raised:
If his father sent שושבינות for him,
when it comes back – it comes back to him.
If שושבינות was sent to his father,
when it is repaid – it is repaid from the middle.
phrases.notes: Here the father owes it, so the debt is paid back out of the shared estate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה of Step 14 with a ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that returned שושבינות is shared by all the brothers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says שושבינות the father sent through a son returns to that son alone

steps.title: The משנה is about gifts sent to the father
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי יוחנן: the משנה is talking about שושבינות sent to the father, which matches the ברייתא's second case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: When we learned the משנה too, we learned it about שושבינות that was sent to the father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by explaining which case the משנה means. It is the case where the father received the gifts, not where he gave them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה is read as gifts sent to the father, it agrees with the ברייתא's second case: the debt is the father's, so it is repaid from the shared estate. The ברייתא's first case, gifts the father sent through a son, is a different case where the son keeps the return.
steps.whatToRemember: שושבינות sent to the father is the father's debt and is repaid from the shared estate. שושבינות the father sent through a son comes back to that son.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: רבי אסי said that רבי יוחנן said:
When we learned our משנה as well,
we learned it about [שושבינות] sent to the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי תְּנַן נָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about שושבינות the father gave
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about שושבינות the father received, matching the ברייתא's second case

steps.title: The wording says the brothers gave the gifts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's reading. The משנה says some of the brothers gave שושבינות, not that someone gave to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'brothers, some of whom gave groomsman gifts'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 16 by pointing to the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the משנה is about gifts that were sent to the father's household. But the words 'some of them made שושבינות' sound like the brothers were the givers. So the wording seems to contradict his reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Groomsman gifts. A gift given at a friend's wedding that he is expected to pay back at the giver's wedding.
It teaches, meaning this is what the text says

phrases.english: But it says "brothers, some of whom made
groomsman gifts"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer from Step 16 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the משנה is about gifts sent to the father's household
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the brothers made (gave) the gifts, which does not fit gifts they received.

steps.title: Read it as 'to some of them'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reading the משנה as 'to some of them': the gifts were given to some of the brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read it as: 'to some of them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes one letter in how the משנה is read, so it now says gifts were brought to some of the brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'למקצתן' (to some of them) in place of 'מקצתן' (some of them), the brothers are the receivers and not the givers. That fits רבי יוחנן's reading exactly.

phrases.english: Read it as: "to some of them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text (changing the wording of the משנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says the brothers gave the gifts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה should read that the gifts were given to some of the brothers.

steps.title: But the משנה says the gift 'came back'
steps.stepSummary: A second wording challenge: the משנה speaks of the שושבינות 'returning', which sounds like the brothers get money back, not that they pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'the groomsman gift returned'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another problem with the wording of the משנה under רבי יוחנן's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the brothers received the gifts, then later they are the ones who must pay them back. But 'the gift returned' sounds like money coming back to them, as if they had been the givers.

phrases.english: But it says "the groomsman gift returned"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Even after the rereading in Step 18, another phrase in the משנה seems not to fit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the brothers were the receivers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Returned' suggests the brothers get paid back, which only makes sense if they were the givers.

steps.title: 'Returned' means it came back to be collected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'returned' means the time came to collect it, and it is collected from the shared estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: when it came back to be collected, it is collected from the middle (the shared estate).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word 'returned' so that it fits paying the gift back instead of getting it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Returned' means the debt came due and the giver came to collect. Because the gift came to the father's household, it is paid out of the shared estate before the brothers divide it, and not by one brother alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The middle, meaning the shared estate of all the brothers

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יוחנן's reading, the משנה is about gifts received in the father's lifetime, and paying them back comes out of the shared estate.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
When it came back to be collected, it is collected from the middle.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: חָזְרָה לִגְבּוֹת – נִגְבֵּית מֵאֶמְצַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 and finishes defending רבי יוחנן's reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Returned' means the brothers get the money back.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Returned' means the debt came due to be collected, and it is paid from the shared estate.

steps.title: רבי אסי: named son versus no son named
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי gives a different answer. The משנה is about gifts the father sent without naming a son, and the ברייתא is about gifts sent for a named son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: There is no difficulty. Here (the משנה) it was sent without saying for whom; there (the ברייתא) it was sent for a named son.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer to the contradiction from Step 15, one that leaves the wording of the משנה as it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources are about gifts the father gave. If he named a son, that son gets the repayment (the ברייתא). If he named no one, the repayment goes to all the brothers together (the משנה).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; both sources can be true

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said: It is not difficult;
here it is without specifying, there it is specified –
phrases.notes: "Here" is the משנה, and "there" is the ברייתא from Step 15.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן בִּסְתָם, כָּאן בִּמְפָרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second way to settle the contradiction from Step 15, separate from the answer in Steps 16-20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא are talking about the same case and disagree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about gifts with no son named; the ברייתא is about gifts sent for a named son.

steps.title: A ברייתא that makes this exact split
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי אסי: gifts sent for a son go back to him; gifts sent without naming anyone go back to the shared estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If his father sent groomsman gifts for him, when it is repaid it is repaid to him. If his father sent gifts without saying for whom, when it is repaid it goes to the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי אסי said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out both cases: a gift naming a son goes back to that son, and an unnamed gift goes back to everyone. This shows that רבי אסי's split is already found in a source.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
It is repaid, it comes back

steps.whatToRemember: Who gets the repayment depends on whether the father named a son when he gave the gift.

phrases.english: As it is taught: If his father sent groomsman gifts for him,
when it is repaid, it is repaid to him.
If his father sent groomsman gifts without specifying,
when it is repaid, it is repaid to the middle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אסי's answer from Step 21 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אסי's split between named and unnamed gifts
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that rules separately on gifts sent for a son and gifts sent without naming anyone

steps.title: שמואל: the case is about a יבם
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains the משנה as being about a יבם. A יבם does not inherit money that was still owed (ראוי) the way he inherits what was already owned (מוחזק).
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Here we are dealing with a יבם, who does not take what is due (ראוי) the same way he takes what was already held (מוחזק).
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer to the contradiction: שמואל places the משנה in a special case involving a יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brother who gave the gifts died without children, and another brother did יבום. When the gifts are repaid, the יבם does not get them alone, because a יבם only inherits what his brother already held, and the repayment was only owed. So the repayment is shared by all the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: A brother who marries the widow of his brother who died without children, and takes his brother's estate
Money that is due but not yet received

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying a יבם inherits nothing. He takes his brother's property that was already held, just not money that was only owed.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Here we are dealing with a yavam,
who does not take what is due as he takes what is held.
phrases.notes: The repayment was only owed to the dead brother, not yet his, so the יבם can't claim it alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the contradiction from Step 15, alongside those of רבי יוחנן and רבי אסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Putting the משנה in a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about an ordinary son who gave gifts, which clashes with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a יבם, who does not inherit ראוי, so the repayment is shared by all the brothers.
steps.whyThisMatters: It uses the general rule that a יבם (like a firstborn) does not inherit ראוי as he inherits מוחזק.

steps.title: Why should the friend repay at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: his answer assumes the friend must still repay. But the friend can say he only owes his own groomsman, who has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean the other one (the friend) has to pay? Let him say: 'Give me my groomsman and I will rejoice with him!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a hidden assumption in שמואל's answer and questions it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's case only works if the friend must repay the gift even though the brother who gave it has died. But שושבינות is paid back by celebrating at the giver's own wedding. Since the giver is dead, the friend should be able to say he owes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The other one (here, the friend who received the gift)
My groomsman, the one who gave me the gift

phrases.english: Does it follow that the other one pays?
phrases.notes: "The other one" is the friend who got the gift from the brother who died.

phrases.english: Let him say: "Give me my groomsman
and I will rejoice with him"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּאִידַּךְ – מְשַׁלֵּם? לֵימָא: ״תְּנוּ לִי שׁוֹשְׁבִינִי וְאֶשְׂמַח עִמּוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what follows from שמואל's answer in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's assumption that the friend must repay after the giver has died
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שושבינות is repaid by celebrating together with the original giver. If he has died, the friend can say there is no one to repay, so no debt is left.

steps.title: A ברייתא about returning betrothal money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: whether קידושין money is returned after a death depends on the local custom.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא: in a place where people usually return the betrothal money, they return it; in a place where people usually don't return it, they don't return it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support its challenge against שמואל. This is the first part of the proof; שמואל's comment on it comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a couple who were betrothed, and then one of them died before the wedding. The ברייתא says local custom decides whether the money is returned. The גמרא will use שמואל's own comment on this ברייתא to strengthen its challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא? (a way of bringing a source as proof)
Betrothal; here, the money or gifts the man gave at the betrothal
A place where people are accustomed (local custom)

phrases.english: Isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
In a place where they are accustomed to return betrothal money, they return it,

phrases.aramaic: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ שֶׁלֹּא לְהַחְזִיר – אֵין מַחְזִירִין.
phrases.english: in a place where they are accustomed not to return it, they do not return it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to back up the challenge in step 24.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge in step 24: the friend can say he only owes his own groomsman, who has died.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about returning קידושין money, together with שמואל's comment on it (next step).

steps.title: שמואל limits the ברייתא to when the woman died
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says that local custom only matters when the woman died. If the man died, the money is never returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף בר אבא said in the name of מר עוקבא in the name of שמואל: they only taught this when she died. But if he died, they do not return the money.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל explains that the ברייתא's 'follow the custom' rule only applies when the woman died. When the man died, nothing is returned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל splits the ברייתא into two cases. If the woman died, we follow the local custom. If the man died, all agree the money stays with her. This ruling comes from שמואל, the same אמורא the גמרא is challenging.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef bar Abba said
that Mar Ukva said that Shmuel said:
They taught this only when she died,
but if he died, they do not return it,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's limit on the ברייתא just quoted, which is the key part of the proof.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Local custom decides only when the woman died. When the man died, the קידושין money is not returned.

steps.title: Why the money stays with her when he died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's ruling and begins the answer: she can make a claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because she can say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the money is not returned when the man died. It begins the answer, 'she can say', and her actual words come in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a setup line. The reason will be a claim she makes about her own side of the deal. That kind of claim is exactly what the friend in step 24 could also make, which would show that שמואל himself accepts it.

keyTerms.meaning: She is able to say (she has a claim)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
She can say:
phrases.notes: Her actual words continue on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind שמואל's ruling in step 26 and begins to give it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the קידושין money is not returned when the man died.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It begins: she has a claim she can make. Her exact words follow in the next lines.
